title: Real World Asset capital is computed by applying the Basel Framework directly, with paragraph-level citations and everything forced into the banking book
content:
For Real World Assets the Atlas does not build a model — it incorporates one. A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.1.1 bases the process on "the Basel Framework developed by the Basel Committee on Bank Supervision," and A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.1.2 sets up a citation grammar (`[Prefix][Chapter].[Paragraph]`, e.g. `CRE20.1`) used throughout, including ranges and sets.

The process is then the standardised-approach pipeline: classify the exposure into one of seven types (on-balance sheet, off-balance sheet, securitization tranches, derivatives/SFTs, funds/CIUs/ETFs, commodities, FX); compute Exposure At Default — book value, or book value × Credit Conversion Factor for off-balance-sheet items — then adjust for Credit Risk Mitigation per `CRE22`; look up risk weights from a table of twenty-plus Basel categories; sum Credit, Market, Counterparty Credit and CVA RWA; apply a leverage adjustment per `CRE99.128-133`; and multiply by an 8% capital ratio (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.2.6).

The most consequential single line is A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.1.3: "all exposures are treated as if they were part of the banking book." In Basel the banking/trading book boundary determines whether an exposure attracts credit-risk capital on amortized value or market-risk capital on mark-to-market moves. Forcing everything into the banking book is a large simplification — it avoids the market-risk regime entirely for assets Sky may in fact trade, understating capital for anything held with short intent, while avoiding the boundary arbitrage that Basel spent two decades fighting.

The fund treatment shows how the framework handles missing information, and it is the same graceful-degradation shape used elsewhere in the Article (A.3.2.2.1.1.1.5.2.3.4): apply the Look Through Approach if look-through is feasible; the Mandate Based Approach if only the mandate is known; otherwise "the fallback conservative approach" per `CRE60.8`. Less information, more capital — never less coverage.

Adopting a supervisory rulebook by reference is a genuine architectural choice with a maintenance consequence: Sky's capital requirements now move when the Basel Committee amends a paragraph, and the Atlas contains no stated process for tracking those amendments.
description: Seven exposure types map to specific CRE/MAR chapters; RWA is EAD times Basel risk weights, leverage-adjusted, times 8% — Sky adopts a supervisory rulebook by reference rather than modeling.
